title: S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Home Price Indices (July 2026 data) — 9:00 a.m. ET, the edition that sets the October print's base
source: EST: the same two primaries the proposing event's canonical file rests on, read for this date rather than October's. (1) press.spglobal.com's June-2026-data release (2026-08-25-S-P-Cotality-Case-Shiller-Index-Reports-Annual-Gain-in-June-2026, fetched direct 2026-09-08, HTTP 200, 90,394 bytes) states the publisher's own rule verbatim: "The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Indices are published on the last Tuesday of each month at 9:00 am ET." September 2026's Tuesdays are the 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th, so the last is 2026-09-29, and the release's own two-month lag (published 2026-08-25 reporting June 2026) puts July 2026 data on it. (2) The Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis's forward calendar for this release, fred.stlouisfed.org/releases/calendar?rid=199 (fetched direct 2026-09-08, HTTP 200), names "September 29, 2026" explicitly. Realized-cadence check made by the proposing lane: all 24 dates on that calendar for 2025 and 2026 are the last Tuesday of their month, and the one apparent exception in the publisher's own newsroom archive (no March 2026 item; the January-2026-data report slugged and datelined 2026-04-28) was resolved as a re-dating artifact, not a missed release — that report's body names "the March 31, 2026, release date" verbatim and a 2026-03-31 ALFRED vintage carrying January-2026 data exists. Filed `estimate` on taxonomy, not date doubt: CONFIRMED_PREFIX in scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs has no member for an index provider's own publication rule. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the case-shiller-hpi-2026-10-27 never-assessed initial research (2026-09-08, D-49), and proposed on exactly the precedent the fhfa-hpi-2026-10-27 lane set when it proposed its own predecessor: this is the edition that SETS the October print's base, and until it lands no August consensus for 10-27 can exist. The proposing lane's central measured finding is what makes it worth a calendar row rather than a mention — because the national index is a three-month moving average, repeating the prior month's m/m forecasts the next one to a 0.119pp MAE (FRED CSUSHPISA, 2015+), so once 09-29 prints July, the August number on 10-27 is pinned about twice as tightly as it is today from June (2-step MAE 0.201pp). The 09-29 edition is also the cleaner slot of the two: it carries FHFA HPI, Consumer Confidence, JOLTS and two Treasury operations, but the September FOMC is 15-16, so unlike 10-27 it is not an FOMC day. Impact `low` and `symbols: []` on the proposing lane's own measurement: no macro- or housing-keyed house playbook (0 hits, 2026-09-08), and across 68 release days since 2021 the 9:00 a.m. print moves no housing instrument's 9:30 open (ITB gap 0.428% vs 0.488% baseline, p=0.4090). WATCH ON THIS EDITION SPECIFICALLY: whether the Wayne County recording-office delay that has suppressed the Detroit index since at least the January-2026 data — restated verbatim in the 2026-08-25 release — is still live. An estimate widens caution; nothing here licenses an entry.
